declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
On behalf of interim class counsel, Hargrove Lane LLP, I submit this statement in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The settlement resulted from successive proposals and counterproposals over five negotiation rounds. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were negotiated concurrently from the opening proposal; fees were not reserved until after agreement on class relief. Counsel initially proposed a $30 million class fund and $5 million in fees and expenses. Brightline initially countered with $23 million for the class and up to $3.5 million in fees and expenses. Subsequent exchanges narrowed both components. After counsel proposed a $25 million class fund with $3.5 million in fees and expenses, Brightline proposed a $24.75 million class fund with the same fee amount, which counsel accepted.

The binding agreement provides a $24.75 million class fund and up to $3.5 million in separately paid, court-approved attorneys’ fees and expenses. The $28.25 million aggregate ceiling includes notice and administration costs, which will be deducted from the class fund rather than paid in addition. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request. Any fees not awarded will supplement the class fund, not revert to Brightline.

Distribution will be automatic, without requiring class members to submit claims. Brightline will supply and reconcile its existing records without charging the fund for its internal cooperation. The agreement includes alternative payment methods for failed credits, reasonable follow-up, feasible redistribution of residual funds, and no reversion of the class fund to Brightline. Notice and administration costs must be reasonable, documented, and subject to an itemized, court-approved budget. No reliable administration estimate was available when the agreement was reached; an administrator quote will be obtained before implementation is finalized. Accordingly, the precise net amount available for class payments is not yet established.

Counsel believes the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate and warrants preliminary approval. The case has survived dismissal, but certification remains unresolved and presents significant risk. Trial would be approximately two to three years away, with recovery uncertain even if certification is obtained. The settlement provides substantial cash relief now, through automatic payments to the identified class, while avoiding those risks and delay. The class fund before administration costs represents approximately 38.7% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges. The absence of a claims requirement promotes participation, and judicial review of fees, the absence of clear sailing, and allocation of any fee reduction to the class provide additional protections. Concurrent negotiation of fees and class relief should nevertheless be considered expressly in evaluating the agreement. Counsel requests preliminary approval subject to the Court’s independent review, an adequate notice process, and further scrutiny of administration costs, distribution procedures, and the fee application before final approval.
